Meta launched a school partnership programme for Instagram last year, promising to prioritise reports submitted by students regarding cyberbullying.

The company has now expanded the programme, allowing schools to publish Stories and notes that can only be viewed by their own students, and supporting the creation of clubs, teams and other functions...

Instagram School Partnership Programme

Instagram's track record on teen mental health is far from ideal. Even the company's own internal research has shown that Instagram may be harming as many as one in five teenage girls, exacerbating their anxieties about physical attractiveness and popularity, among other things.

Cyberbullying has long been one of the major issues facing teenage users of social platforms, and it was for this reason that Meta launched a programme last year aimed at helping schools deal with the problem. Once a school signs up for the partnership, Meta promises to prioritise reports submitted by students and staff.

New School Features

Meta said today it was adding a number of new features to the programme.

Channels. Allow schools to share the latest updates with parents and students; only school admins can post messages within a channel.

School Stories and notes. Both staff and students can post, viewable only by authenticated students of that school. School admins can remove the relevant content.

Clubs and Teams. Anyone in the school can set up a club or team, serving as a centralised hub for posting about related activities and information.

Student directory. Students can use the platform to look up other students' contact details within the school, visible only to other students and to teen followers who follow each other.

Meta noted that these new features are intended for use outside classroom hours, and emphasised that teen accounts allow parents to block access during school hours.

High school student identity verification is handled by UNiDAYS, the same company Apple uses to provide verified educational pricing.
